citation: Klise, K.A., Bynum, M., Moriarty, D., Murray, R. (2017). A software framework for assessing the resilience of drinking water systems to disasters with an example earthquake case study. Environmental Modelling and Software 95, 420-431. doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2017.06.022

dedupe_keys.name: water network tool for resilience wntr

description: WNTR is a Python package that simulates and analyses the resilience of drinking water distribution networks to disasters. It reads and writes EPANET input files, lets users build or modify network structure and operations, and adds disruptive events such as pipe leaks, power outages, damage to tanks, valves and pumps, contaminant injection and environmental change, with component failure drawn from fragility curves. Repair and response strategies can then be applied, and the network is simulated with demand-driven or pressure-dependent hydraulics and water quality through EPANET or WNTR's own Python simulator. Results are summarised with topographic, hydraulic, water quality and security, and economic resilience metrics and plotted. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Research and Development developed it with Sandia National Laboratories to bring the main pieces of water-system resilience modelling into one framework. It is generic: any network, anywhere, described as an EPANET model can be studied, and the repository ships example networks. It is distributed through the USEPA GitHub organisation, PyPI and conda-forge; version 1.5.0 was released on 1 July 2026. Licence: Revised BSD, free to use. Caveats: results depend on the quality of the utility's EPANET model and of the fragility curves supplied, which WNTR does not provide for a specific place. Simulation uses: resilience analysis, network flow, cascading failure through power dependencies, emergency response and hazard exposure such as earthquakes. It builds on the EPANET engine catalogued as model-epanet and complements network-optimisation packages such as WaterModels.
